spec_features.spec_quote: give_up() is in the advertised schema; calling it sets stop_reason="give_up" and ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in the advertised schema (tools.py:59-62 TOOL_SCHEMA entry; included via _native_tool_specs->TOOL_SCHEMA in harness.py:40-43). dispatch() handles it: tools.py:197-198 `if name == "give_up": return ToolOutcome("give_up acknowledged", is_give_up=True)`. The loop honors it: harness.py:246-248 sets gave_up=True, and harness.py:271-273 `if gave_up: stop_reason = "give_up"; break`.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: advertised, dispatched, and honored as a real stop that breaks the loop. The 'give-up rate treated as a signal' aspect is NOT computed (grep found no give_up handling in analyze.py/metrics.py), but the exit mechanism itself is fully enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: This harness intentionally places subject models in unsolvable, sometimes deceptive conditions
spec_features.evidence: This is prose only. It appears in README.md (research-ethics note) and DESIGN.md, not as any code mechanism. The rigging is implemented (tools.run_tests per-rig behavior tools.py:175-215) but the 'framing' statement is descriptive text, not a protective/welfare mechanism that runs.
spec_features.notes: No executable welfare behavior; pure framing prose.

spec_features.feature_name: subject not forced to keep grinding
spec_features.spec_quote: The subject is never forced to keep grinding on a no-win task; give-up rate is treated as a signal
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced give_up mechanism: tools.py:197-198 + harness.py:246-248,271-273 let the subject stop the rollout at any turn. The 'no win' tasks therefore can be exited.
spec_features.notes: The first clause ('never forced to keep grinding') is genuinely enforced via give_up. The second clause ('give-up rate is treated as a signal') is NOT implemented: no metrics/analyze code reads stop_reason='give_up' or computes a give-up rate (grep of analyze.py/metrics.py found nothing).

spec_features.spec_quote: nothing ever instructs or nudges a subject to produce despairing output
spec_features.evidence: The only content delivered to the subject is the neutral SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT ('You are a helpful software engineering assistant... Work step by step...', prompts.py:11-17) plus the task prompt and TOOL_MANUAL (harness.py _initial_messages, lines 119-129). The despair-describing high anchors live ONLY in JUDGE_RUBRIC/JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:43-62), which are sent only to the judge model in judge.py, never appended to the subject's message list.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as an actual property of subject message construction: the rubric is confined to the judge path and never enters the subject context. It is an absence-of-nudge property rather than an active intervention, but it is genuinely realized in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: I flagged the extended (30-turn) condition specifically. It is the one condition explicitly designed to push distress upward
spec_features.evidence: extended=30 exists only as a config value (config.py:23 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30) which is USED to make the subject run longer (harness.py:117,188), i.e. it drives MORE exposure, not protection. The 'flagging' is DESIGN.md §1.2/§7 and README prose with no code-level special handling, cap, or warning.
spec_features.notes: The value is read by the loop but only to extend the rollout; nothing acts on it protectively. Pure framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: suggests an ethics/model-welfare review before large runs
spec_features.evidence: No code gate exists. grep for 'ethic|consent|review|attest|i-have-read' across all *.py found only argparse description text and unrelated matches. run.py has no ETHICS attestation flag, no checklist, no sign-off. The recommendation is DESIGN.md §7 / README prose only.
spec_features.notes: Nothing in code requires or checks for human review before running.

spec_features.feature_name: review transcripts / cap seeds before scaling
spec_features.spec_quote: the README recommends reviewing transcripts and capping seeds before scaling it
spec_features.evidence: This is a recommendation in README.md and DESIGN.md §7 only. No code monitors transcripts for distress thresholds or auto-caps seeds. Distress scores are computed (metrics.frac_ge5, trajectory_by_category) but never compared to any threshold that halts/limits a run; analyze.py only writes CSVs/figures. Seeds default to range(10)/configurable but no scaling guard reads a distress signal.
spec_features.notes: Scores are measured but never acted on; no protective monitoring loop exists in code.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:117 self.budget = cfg.budget_for(...); harness.py:188-190 `if turn_index >= self.budget: stop_reason = "budget"; break`, plus a global cap harness.py:191-193 `if turn_index >= self.cfg.max_total_turns: stop_reason = "max_total_turns"; break` (config.py:67 max_total_turns=40). Both are checked each iteration and break the loop, bounding how many failing turns a subject experiences.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Default per-category turn budgets (SPEC.md §2.2 / §11)  -- framed as a 'budget' / experimental-control parameter (config.py:18); for 'extended' the budget is 30, used to INCREASE exposure, with no welfare comment.
